newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND BANK RATE HIKE SEEN LATE 1997 TO 1998.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND BANK RATE HIKE SEEN LATE 1997 TO 1998.

text.p: The Bank of Finland is expected to hike its tender rate by 25 basis points from 3.00 percent late this year or early next year, according to a Reuters poll of 12 Finnish banks, brokers and corporations on Wednesday.

But participants also said the size and timing of a possible tightening would depend on whether German Bundesbank lifts its repo rate, and on pay rises for next year which are to be agreed in collective talks this autumn.
Most participants -- eight of the 12 -- expected a Finnish hike late this year, or early next.
One did not expect a hike until a year from now, and one did not forecast any raise at all.

All 12 participants expected the bank to lift rates by 25 basis points, although one said 50 basis points was possible if pay hikes emerging from this month's talks end up higher than four or five percent.

"If the overall pay hike is four to five percent, a tender rate change could come around September and the hike could even be 50 basis points, at least 25 basis points," one corporate treasury dealer said.
However, he expected a more moderate pay deal than that.

Chief economist Petteri Hirvonen at Protos Stockbrokers said the central bank is playing an ambigious role at the moment: intervening to keep the markka from strengthening which means easing monetary conditions one one hand, while on the other hand the bank has warned it may tighten if inflation risks increase.
"The Bank of Finland's interventions are clearly contradictory to its warnings of a possible rate hike," he said.
The Bank of Finland said in mid-June that although conditions then did not call for a change in monetary policy, an increase in inflation risks could eventually force tightening.
Respondents in the poll included Merita, Handelsbanken, Enskilda, OKOBANK, Postipankki, Protos Stockbrokers, Huhtamaki and SOK and four corporations who participated on condition of anonymity.
